newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices fall as U.S. stocks turn market bearish.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices fall as U.S. stocks turn market bearish.

text.p: Oil prices fell on Wednesday as a weather-led rally was scuppered by U.S. stocks data showing a sharp rise in heating oil inventories in the world's leading energy consuming nation.
In London, February futures for world marker crude Brent Blend, fell to an intra-day low of $24.22 a barrel and at 1612 GMT were trading 21 cents lower at $24.38.

Oil prices started the year with a strong rally on the back of freezing weather across Europe, which boosted gas oil (used in Europe for heating purposes) values and put a firm floor under crude oil prices.
Front-month Brent rose steadily from the beginning of January, gaining nearly $1 a barrel despite the resumption of Iraqi crude oil exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal three weeks ago.

Brokers said the cold weather factor had been used up by the market and the main driver on Wednesday was publication of U.S. inventory data showing a 2.94 million barrel build in distillates stocks (which include heating oil) last week.

"Overall, there may be further products-induced losses today, but there is probably not enough in this data to give the bears the upper hand for long from a fundamental viewpoint," said brokers GNI Research in a daily report.
The New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) led the London market lower and brokers said any sign of a thaw in Europe would be a signal to sell.

Brokers at GNI and Prudential Bache in London said the potentially bullish news that U.S. crude oil stocks held in primary storage fell 9.47 million barrels in the week ending January 3 should be seen in the context of end of year tax considerations.

"The crude draw is less positive than the headline figure for a couple of reasons. First, end of year tax considerations have played a role, and there have been problems with the weather conditions in the U.S. Gulf, which have disrupted loadings," GNI said.

Despite weekly fluctuations in U.S. stock levels, inventories are overall lower than year-ago levels and low industry stocks in consuming countries were the main reason for pushing oil prices to a near six-year high in October last year.

The Iraqi crude which started flowing into the market on December 16 under the U.N. limited oil sales deal has been absorbed by a tight winter market. U.N. sources said on Tuesday Iraqi exports would peak in late February/ early March to around 618,000 barrels per day (bpd).

Iraq has been under U.N. sanctions since its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait. Under the partial sales plan, Baghdad will be allowed to export $2 billion worth of crude oil over six months to pay for food and medicines.
